- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model underreacts; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion.  
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply 1–2% downward adjustment for first 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is positive but volatile (e.g., alternating +/–0.3), model tends to smooth too much; allow 1–2% upward bias in forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after model peak, model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 5–7 days if sentiment turns negative.
